title: Stay Calm. Remain Indoors. Dev Diary #4 : Reset #1
author: AsparagusOk8818
selftext:
After an aggravating afternoon of playtesting, I decided to reset the visual direction of SCRI to a slightly earlier version.

The ASCII is extremely easy to work with, so I'm extremely sad to see it go... but I just couldn't get the right feeling of play through it. The theater of the mind wasn't being expressed through the mechanics like I had hoped it would, at least for me. 

  
So, I'm on the 256 color pixel sprite train. On the bright side, I do get to use this parallax opening screen I'm kind of fond of (the backgrounds and the JACL tanks are not AI-generated; the backgrounds were purchased from [Craftpix.com](http://Craftpix.com), while the JACL is a modification made to Erick Javier and Shimmering-Sword's depiction of the Conservator-class Bolo; one of my favorite pieces of art I've ever been given permission to use and modify. 

Just FYI, if you want parallax backgrounds, both Claude and Astra (and Sol for that matter) know how to make it work so long as you have the correct images to lay on top of each other. I'm skeptical that they could make good parallax images themselves but I haven't tried it lately.   


On the down side.... I'm back to wrestling with ChatGPT imagegen. I genuinely don't personally care about the 'AI look' of things, but I do care that things look right, and that's just so hard to do with the current tools IMHO.  
  
  
I'll share some current process / workflow related content in a reply below since I know I'm always personally interested in that and presumably other folks are too.

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
https://preview.redd.it/anjac78q66vh1.png?width=1521&format=png&auto=webp&s=6480d56a50b8846dc6cef94800bbc6417d3edc65

Environments are the toughest thing for me. 

My current plan here is to divide this stage graphic that imagegen created for me into the foreground and middle ground, where the trees will be able to layer on top of some elements that will occassionally drive in front of the furtherest backdrop image. Trains, big tanks, aircraft, etc. 

Grids will be 6 x 12, with each cell being 96 x 96 px. The stage foreground, middle ground and background layers will be cut and cropped into equal 576 x 1152 pieces. 

  
I'll copy and paste an example of how I build my sprites in case anyone's interested in the specifics of the prompts: 

'@create image

Pixel art, 32-bit

Please draw 12 variations of this concept in a 4 x 3 grid with a transparent background, with each variation occupying 1 cell of the grid:

A massive male ogre with deep purple skin, with bright and colorful tattoos on his arm depicting a mountain and river. He is hyper-muscular, with oversized biceps, forearms and hands. He has massive tusks and proportionately small, narrow eyes that glow orange.

He is wearing a ronin outfit - a hakama and a kosode - and a black Jingasa with a pink lotus crest on it.

The ogre has long white hair.

The ogre should be wielding a club with their far hand, resting it against their far shoulder.'

  
Sprites are then cut out of the sheet and processed at [portalrabbit.com](https://portalrabbit.com/). 

  
For environments, here's an example prompt: 

'@create image  
  
environmental belt-scroller pixel art.  
  
A dirt road cutting straight and horizontally through a lush, dense jungle with colossally huge trees.  
  
This image should represent the middle layer that could be part of a 3 layer image, meant to later accomodate a foreground and background layer. The dirt road should represent a laver stage as be unobstructed by foreground elements (as those would be added later), and the background behind this middle layer should be bright solid color mask that could be easily isolated, selected and removed.'

  
...You can probably ask it to just make the background transparent, but I was having trouble with it at the time so just made it magenta, then reduced colors to 8, selected the magenta, kicked the colors back to RGB and re-pasted the image onto the selection so I could delete punch the transparency through cleanly.

Then ran the image through this tool: 

[Free AI Pixel Art Fixer | Sprite Fusion Pixel Snapper](https://www.spritefusion.com/pixel-snapper)

Then upscaled it x5. 

  
Getting cityscapes to not look like total crap is a nightmare, but stuff like jungles and deserts seem to work okay most of the time.
